question: Find the part of the sentence containing an error: Were he to have acted sooner (1)/ the situation might have been (2)/ resolved long before it escalated (3)/ preventing further issues (4).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part 1: "**Were he to have acted sooner**."
 
• The phrase "**Were he to have acted sooner**" is incorrect because the phrase "**were he**" is typically used in conditional sentences for hypothetical scenarios, but the addition of "**to have acted**" complicates the construction and makes it ungrammatical.
 
• The correct phrase should simply be "**Had he acted sooner**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Had he acted sooner, the situation might have been resolved long before it escalated, preventing further issues."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 2: "the situation might have been" **– This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 3: "resolved long before it escalated"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 4: "preventing further issues"** – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
